content.text: The text combines romantic and colonial-era poems with extensive biographical and scientific prose. The poems explore love, desire, separation, mortality, war, race, duty, and nature, set across India, Burma, Afghanistan, and the Malay world. A long biography portrays Thomas Paine’s political writings, religious skepticism, inventions, friendships, persecution, illness, death in Greenwich, New York, burial at New Rochelle, and later cultural influence. It records Paine’s movements from England to Philadelphia, France, America, New York, New Rochelle, and other places, including his imprisonment in Luxembourg and residence with the Bonnevilles. Appendices add firsthand recollections, letters, portraits, and mechanical experiments. The final natural-history sections describe Osmia bees’ sex allocation, Glow-worm predation and bioluminescence, cabbage-caterpillar development, and Microgaster wasps parasitizing caterpillar eggs.
